quotes.zh: 再聪明的人，也看不清自己所做的全部恶事。
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.en: We always love those who admire us, and we do not always love those whom we admire.
quotes.zh: 我们总爱那些欣赏我们的人，却不总爱我们所欣赏的人。
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.en: We promise according to our hopes, and perform according to our fears.
quotes.zh: 我们按希望许诺，却按恐惧履行。
quotes.author: La Rochefoucauld

quotes.en: Power should be a check to power.
quotes.zh: 权力应当以权力来制约。
quotes.author: Montesquieu

quotes.en: There is no greater tyranny than that which is perpetrated under the shield of the law.
quotes.zh: 没有比披着法律外衣施行的暴政更大的暴政。
quotes.author: Montesquieu

quotes.en: Laws should be adapted to the people for whom they are made.
quotes.zh: 法律应当适应它所服务的人民。
quotes.author: Montesquieu

quotes.en: Useless laws weaken necessary laws.
quotes.zh: 无用的法律会削弱必要的法律。
quotes.author: Montesquieu

quotes.en: In a republic, virtue is the foundation of the state.
quotes.zh: 在共和国里，美德是国家的基础。
quotes.author: Montesquieu

quotes.en: The spirit of moderation ought to be that of the legislator.
quotes.zh: 立法者的精神应当是适度的精神。
quotes.author: Montesquieu

quotes.en: Only passions, great passions, can elevate the soul to great things.
quotes.zh: 只有激情，伟大的激情，才能把灵魂提升到伟大的事物。
quotes.author: Denis Diderot

quotes.en: The first step towards philosophy is incredulity.
quotes.zh: 迈向哲学的第一步是怀疑。
quotes.author: Denis Diderot

quotes.en: All things must be examined, debated, and investigated without exception.
quotes.zh: 一切事物都应毫无例外地被审视、辩论和探究。
quotes.author: Denis Diderot

quotes.en: There is no moral precept that does not have something inconvenient about it.
quotes.zh: 没有哪条道德训诫不带着某种不便。
quotes.author: Denis Diderot

quotes.en: It is a great misfortune not to have enough wit to speak well, or not enough judgment to keep silent.
quotes.zh: 既没有足够的才思把话说好，又没有足够的判断力保持沉默，是极大的不幸。
quotes.author: La Bruyère

quotes.en: The pleasure of criticism deprives us of the pleasure of being moved by beautiful things.
quotes.zh: 挑剔的乐趣，会夺走我们被美好事物打动的乐趣。
quotes.author: La Bruyère

quotes.en: Life is a tragedy for those who feel and a comedy for those who think.
quotes.zh: 对感受者，人生是悲剧；对思考者，人生是喜剧。
quotes.author: La Bruyère

quotes.en: There is nothing like a dream to create the future.
quotes.zh: 没有什么比梦想更能创造未来。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: There is nothing more powerful than an idea whose time has come.
quotes.zh: 没有什么比一个时机已到的思想更有力量。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: The greatest happiness of life is the conviction that we are loved.
quotes.zh: 人生最大的幸福，是确信自己被人爱着。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: Music expresses that which cannot be said and on which it is impossible to be silent.
quotes.zh: 音乐表达的是无法言说、却又无法沉默以对的东西。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: He who opens a school door, closes a prison.
quotes.zh: 打开一扇校门的人，就关上了一个牢门。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: Laughter is sunshine; it chases winter from the human face.
quotes.zh: 笑声是阳光，它把冬天从人脸上赶走。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: The beautiful is as useful as the useful; perhaps more so.
quotes.zh: 美和有用一样有用，也许还更有用。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: It is nothing to die; it is frightful not to live.
quotes.zh: 死算不了什么；可怕的是不曾真正活过。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: While ignorance and poverty remain on earth, books of this kind cannot be useless.
quotes.zh: 只要世上还有愚昧与贫困，这样的书就不会无用。
quotes.author: Victor Hugo

quotes.en: The mind is its own place, and in itself can make a heaven of hell, a hell of heaven.
quotes.zh: 心灵自有其处所，它能把地狱变成天堂，也能把天堂变成地狱。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: Better to reign in hell than serve in heaven.
quotes.zh: 宁在地狱称王，不在天堂为奴。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: They also serve who only stand and wait.
quotes.zh: 只是站立等待的人，也在服侍。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: Awake, arise, or be forever fallen.
quotes.zh: 醒来，起身，否则就永远沉沦。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: The end of learning is to repair the ruins of our own natures.
quotes.zh: 学习的目的是修补我们天性中的残破。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: He who reigns within himself and rules passions, desires, and fears is more than a king.
quotes.zh: 能统御自己、管住激情、欲望与恐惧的人，胜过国王。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: What is strength without a double share of wisdom?
quotes.zh: 没有双份智慧相伴的力量，算得了什么？
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: Peace hath her victories no less renowned than war.
quotes.zh: 和平的胜利，与战争的胜利同样光荣。
quotes.author: John Milton

quotes.en: He that is down needs fear no fall.
quotes.zh: 已经跌到底的人，不必再怕跌倒。
quotes.author: John Bunyan

quotes.en: Be of good cheer, my brother, for I feel the bottom, and it is sound.
quotes.zh: 振作起来，兄弟，我摸到了河底，它是坚实的。
quotes.author: John Bunyan

quotes.en: To err is human; to forgive, divine.
quotes.zh: 犯错是人之常情，宽恕才是神圣。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: A little learning is a dangerous thing.
quotes.zh: 一知半解是危险的事。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Hope springs eternal in the human breast.
quotes.zh: 希望永远在人心底涌出。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: The proper study of mankind is man.
quotes.zh: 人类恰当的研究对象是人。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread.
quotes.zh: 天使不敢踏足之处，愚人却贸然闯入。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: True wit is nature to advantage dressed.
quotes.zh: 真正的机智，是打扮得更美的自然。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Be silent always when you doubt your sense.
quotes.zh: 拿不准自己判断时，就保持沉默。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Men must be taught as if you taught them not.
quotes.zh: 教人时，要让人感觉不到你在教。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Order is heaven's first law.
quotes.zh: 秩序是上天的第一条法则。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Vice is a monster of so frightful mien, as to be hated needs but to be seen.
quotes.zh: 恶习是个面目可憎的怪物，只要看见就足以令人憎恶。
quotes.author: Alexander Pope

quotes.en: Satire is a sort of glass wherein beholders do generally discover everybody's face but their own.
quotes.zh: 讽刺是一面镜子，看的人往往照见别人的脸，唯独照不见自己的。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: When a true genius appears in the world, you may know him by this sign, that the dunces are all in confederacy against him.
quotes.zh: 真正的天才出现时，你可以凭这个迹象认出他：蠢人们都联合起来对付他。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: We have just enough religion to make us hate, but not enough to make us love one another.
quotes.zh: 我们的宗教刚好够让我们彼此仇恨，却不够让我们彼此相爱。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: Every man desires to live long, but no man wishes to be old.
quotes.zh: 人人都想长寿，却没人愿意变老。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: Laws are cobwebs which may catch small flies, but let wasps and hornets break through.
quotes.zh: 法律像蛛网，能捉住小苍蝇，却让黄蜂和大马蜂破网而过。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: Vision is the art of seeing things invisible.
quotes.zh: 远见，就是看见看不见之物的艺术。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: It is useless to attempt to reason a man out of a thing he was never reasoned into.
quotes.zh: 想用道理说服一个人放弃他从未用道理接受的东西，是徒劳的。
quotes.author: Jonathan Swift

quotes.en: Hell is paved with good intentions.
quotes.zh: 地狱是用好心肠铺成的。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: When a man is tired of London, he is tired of life.
quotes.zh: 一个人厌倦了伦敦，就是厌倦了生活。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Patriotism is the last refuge of a scoundrel.
quotes.zh: 爱国主义是恶棍最后的避难所。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: To be happy at home is the ultimate result of all ambition.
quotes.zh: 在家中得到幸福，是一切抱负的最终结果。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Curiosity is one of the permanent and certain characteristics of a vigorous intellect.
quotes.zh: 好奇心是旺盛智力永久而确定的特征之一。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Great works are performed not by strength but by perseverance.
quotes.zh: 伟大的事业不是靠力量，而是靠坚持完成的。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Dictionaries are like watches; the worst is better than none, and the best cannot be expected to go quite true.
quotes.zh: 词典像钟表：最差的也比没有好，最好的也别指望走得完全准。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Read over your compositions, and wherever you meet with a passage which you think is particularly fine, strike it out.
quotes.zh: 重读你的文章，凡是遇到你自觉得意之笔，就把它划掉。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Knowledge is more than equivalent to force.
quotes.zh: 知识的力量胜过暴力。
quotes.author: Samuel Johnson

quotes.en: Great wits are sure to madness near allied, and thin partitions do their bounds divide.
quotes.zh: 伟大的才子必与疯狂相近，两者之间只隔一层薄板。
quotes.author: John Dryden

quotes.en: None but the brave deserve the fair.
quotes.zh: 唯有勇敢者才配得上美好。
quotes.author: John Dryden

quotes.en: Music hath charms to soothe a savage breast.
quotes.zh: 音乐有魅力，能安抚野蛮的心胸。
quotes.author: John Dryden

quotes.en: What passion cannot music raise and quell?
quotes.zh: 有什么激情是音乐不能激起、又不能平息的？
quotes.author: John Dryden

quotes.en: What sunshine is to flowers, smiles are to humanity.
quotes.zh: 微笑之于人，正如阳光之于花。
quotes.author: Joseph Addison

quotes.en: A contented mind is the greatest blessing a man can enjoy in this world.
quotes.zh: 知足的心，是人在世上能享有的最大福分。
quotes.author: Joseph Addison

quotes.en: Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body.
quotes.zh: 读书之于心灵，犹如运动之于身体。
quotes.author: Joseph Addison

quotes.en: Our real blessings often appear to us in the shape of pains, losses and disappointments.
quotes.zh: 真正的福分，常以痛苦、损失和失望的样子来到我们面前。
quotes.author: Joseph Addison

quotes.en: The age of chivalry is gone.
quotes.zh: 骑士时代已经过去了。
quotes.author: Edmund Burke
quotes.source: Reflections on the Revolution in France

quotes.en: A state without the means of some change is without the means of its conservation.
quotes.zh: 一个国家若没有一些变革的手段，也就没有保全自己的手段。
quotes.author: Edmund Burke
quotes.source: Reflections on the Revolution in France

quotes.en: Society is indeed a contract.
quotes.zh: 社会确实是一种契约。
quotes.author: Edmund Burke
quotes.source: Reflections on the Revolution in France

quotes.en: Government is a contrivance of human wisdom to provide for human wants.
quotes.zh: 政府是人类智慧为满足人类需要而设计的装置。
quotes.author: Edmund Burke
quotes.source: Reflections on the Revolution in France

quotes.en: Our patience will achieve more than our force.
quotes.zh: 我们的耐心能成就的，比武力更多。
quotes.author: Edmund Burke

quotes.en: The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.
quotes.zh: 邪恶获胜的唯一条件，就是好人袖手旁观。
quotes.author: Edmund Burke

quotes.en: I have called this principle, by which each slight variation, if useful, is preserved, by the term natural selection.
quotes.zh: 我把这一原理称为自然选择：凡是有用的微小变异都会被保存下来。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: There is a grandeur in this view of life.
quotes.zh: 这种生命观中蕴含着壮丽。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: From so simple a beginning, endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved.
quotes.zh: 从如此简单的起点，无数最美丽、最奇妙的形态已经演化出来，并且仍在演化。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: We see beautiful adaptations everywhere and in every part of the organic world.
quotes.zh: 在有机世界的每个角落，我们都能看到美妙的适应。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: I am fully convinced that species are not immutable.
quotes.zh: 我完全确信，物种并非一成不变。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: The love for all living creatures is the most noble attribute of man.
quotes.zh: 对一切生灵的爱，是人类最高贵的品质。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
quotes.zh: 无知比知识更容易生出自信。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: False facts are highly injurious to the progress of science, for they often endure long.
quotes.zh: 虚假的事实对科学进步危害极大，因为它们往往长久流传。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: The highest possible stage in moral culture is when we recognize that we ought to control our thoughts.
quotes.zh: 道德修养的最高阶段，是我们认识到应当控制自己的思想。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: The difference in mind between man and the higher animals is certainly one of degree and not of kind.
quotes.zh: 人与高等动物在心智上的差别，肯定是程度之别，而非种类之别。
quotes.author: Charles Darwin

quotes.en: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
quotes.zh: 如果我看得更远，那是因为我站在巨人的肩上。
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.en: Truth is ever to be found in simplicity, and not in the multiplicity and confusion of things.
quotes.zh: 真理总是在简单之中，而不在事物的繁多与混乱之中。
quotes.author: Isaac Newton
quotes.source: Rules for the Study of Natural Philosophy

quotes.en: We are to admit no more causes of natural things than such as are both true and sufficient to explain their appearances.
quotes.zh: 对于自然事物，我们只应承认那些既真实又足以解释其现象的成因。
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.en: To every action there is always opposed an equal reaction.
quotes.zh: 每一个作用力，总有一个大小相等的反作用力与之相对。
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.en: What we know is a drop, what we don't know is an ocean.
quotes.zh: 我们所知的只是一滴水，我们所不知的却是一片海洋。
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.en: I can calculate the motion of heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people.
quotes.zh: 我能计算天体的运动，却算不出人心的疯狂。
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.en: And yet it moves.
quotes.zh: 可它仍在转动。
quotes.author: Galileo Galilei

quotes.en: The book of nature is written in the language of mathematics.
quotes.zh: 自然之书是用数学的语言写成的。
quotes.author: Galileo Galilei

quotes.en: Measure what is measurable, and make measurable what is not so.
quotes.zh: 测量可测量之物，并把不可测量之物也变得可测量。
quotes.author: Galileo Galilei

quotes.en: All truths are easy to understand once they are discovered; the point is to discover them.
quotes.zh: 一切真理一旦被发现都容易理解，关键在于发现它们。
quotes.author: Galileo Galilei

quotes.en: In questions of science, the authority of a thousand is not worth the humble reasoning of a single individual.
quotes.zh: 在科学问题上，一千人的权威也比不上一个人谦卑的推理。
quotes.author: Galileo Galilei

quotes.en: At rest, however, in the middle of everything is the sun.
quotes.zh: 然而，在万物中央静止不动的，是太阳。
quotes.author: Nicolaus Copernicus

quotes.en: I am not so fond of my own opinions as to disregard what others think.
quotes.zh: 我并不至于偏爱自己的见解，而无视别人的想法。
quotes.author: Nicolaus Copernicus

quotes.en: Mathematics is written for mathematicians.
quotes.zh: 数学是写给数学家的。
quotes.author: Nicolaus Copernicus

quotes.en: I was merely thinking God's thoughts after him.
quotes.zh: 我只是在追随上帝的思路而已。
quotes.author: Johannes Kepler

quotes.en: Geometry is one and eternal shining in the mind of God.
quotes.zh: 几何是上帝心中唯一而永恒的光辉。
quotes.author: Johannes Kepler

quotes.en: Nature loves simplicity and unity.
quotes.zh: 自然喜爱简单与统一。
quotes.author: Johannes Kepler

quotes.en: I much prefer the sharpest criticism of a single intelligent man to the thoughtless approval of the masses.
quotes.zh: 我宁愿要一个智者最尖锐的批评，也不要大众不加思索的赞同。
quotes.author: Johannes Kepler

quotes.en: Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.
quotes.zh: 只要符合自然规律，再奇妙的事也不会不真实。
quotes.author: Michael Faraday

quotes.en: Nature is our kindest friend and best critic in experimental science if we only allow her intimations to fall unbiased on our minds.
quotes.zh: 在实验科学中，自然是我们最友善的朋友和最好的批评者，只要我们让她的暗示不带偏见地落入心中。
quotes.author: Michael Faraday

quotes.en: But still try, for who knows what is possible?
quotes.zh: 仍要去尝试，谁知道什么才是可能的呢？
quotes.author: Michael Faraday

quotes.en: Work. Finish. Publish.
quotes.zh: 去做，做完，发表。
quotes.author: Michael Faraday

quotes.en: Try to learn something about everything and everything about something.
quotes.zh: 试着对一切都懂一点，对某一点懂一切。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: The great tragedy of science is the slaying of a beautiful hypothesis by an ugly fact.
quotes.zh: 科学的大悲剧，就是一个丑陋的事实杀死了美丽的假说。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: The known is finite, the unknown infinite; intellectually we stand on an islet in the midst of an illimitable ocean of inexplicability.
quotes.zh: 已知有限，未知无穷；在智识上，我们站在无法解释的无垠海洋中的一座小岛上。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley
quotes.source: On the Reception of the Origin of Species

quotes.en: Education is the instruction of the intellect in the laws of Nature.
quotes.zh: 教育就是让智识学习自然规律。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: Sit down before fact as a little child, be prepared to give up every preconceived notion.
quotes.zh: 像孩子一样坐在事实面前，准备好放弃一切先入之见。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: The deepest sin against the human mind is to believe things without evidence.
quotes.zh: 对人类心智最深重的罪，是相信没有证据的东西。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: Logical consequences are the scarecrows of fools and the beacons of wise men.
quotes.zh: 逻辑的结论是愚人的稻草人，是智者的灯塔。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: The great end of life is not knowledge but action.
quotes.zh: 人生的伟大目标不是知识，而是行动。
quotes.author: Thomas Henry Huxley

quotes.en: The art of being wise is the art of knowing what to overlook.
quotes.zh: 智慧的艺术，就是懂得什么该忽略的艺术。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Believe that life is worth living, and your belief will help create the fact.
quotes.zh: 相信生活值得过，你的信念就会帮你把它变成事实。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Nothing is so fatiguing as the eternal hanging on of an uncompleted task.
quotes.zh: 没有什么比一件永远未完成的事更让人疲惫。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: A great many people think they are thinking when they are merely rearranging their prejudices.
quotes.zh: 很多人以为自己在思考，其实只是在重新排列自己的偏见。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Habit is thus the enormous fly-wheel of society.
quotes.zh: 习惯于是成了社会巨大的飞轮。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: The greatest discovery of my generation is that a human being can alter his life by altering his attitudes.
quotes.zh: 我们这一代最伟大的发现是，人可以通过改变态度来改变生活。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Act as if what you do makes a difference. It does.
quotes.zh: 就当你的所作所为能带来改变那样去行动。它确实能。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Acceptance of what has happened is the first step to overcoming the consequences of any misfortune.
quotes.zh: 接受已发生的事，是克服任何不幸后果的第一步。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Genius is only a superior power of seeing.
quotes.zh: 天才不过是一种更强大的看见的能力。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: Our faith in a fact can help create the fact.
quotes.zh: 我们对一个事实的信念，能帮助这个事实成真。
quotes.author: William James

quotes.en: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife.
quotes.zh: 有一条举世公认的真理：一个拥有丰厚家产的单身男子，必定缺一位妻子。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: There is no charm equal to tenderness of heart.
quotes.zh: 没有什么魅力能胜过一颗温柔的心。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: We have all a better guide in ourselves, if we would attend to it, than any other person can be.
quotes.zh: 只要我们肯倾听，自己心里就有一位比任何人都好的向导。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: Vanity working on a weak head produces every sort of mischief.
quotes.zh: 虚荣心作祟于一个孱弱的头脑，会生出各种祸端。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: The person, be it gentleman or lady, who has not pleasure in a good novel, must be intolerably stupid.
quotes.zh: 无论男女，若不能从一部好小说中获得乐趣，必定愚不可耐。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: One half of the world cannot understand the pleasures of the other.
quotes.zh: 世上有一半人无法理解另一半人的乐趣。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: There is nothing like staying at home for real comfort.
quotes.zh: 要想真正舒适，没有什么比得上待在家里。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: If I loved you less, I might be able to talk about it more.
quotes.zh: 我若爱你少一些，也许就能多谈一些。
quotes.author: Jane Austen

quotes.en: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
quotes.zh: 那是最好的时代，也是最坏的时代。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done.
quotes.zh: 我现在做的事，远比我做过的任何事都好。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of it to anyone else.
quotes.zh: 凡是能减轻他人负担的人，在这世上都不是无用的。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: There are dark shadows on the earth, but its lights are stronger in the contrast.
quotes.zh: 世上确有黑暗的阴影，但正因对比，光明才更强。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure nineteen six, result happiness.
quotes.zh: 年收入二十镑，年支出十九镑六先令，结果就是幸福。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.
quotes.zh: 我要在心里敬守圣诞，并努力整年保持这份心意。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: Mankind was my business.
quotes.zh: 人类就是我的事业。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: The pain of parting is nothing to the joy of meeting again.
quotes.zh: 离别的痛苦，比起重逢的喜悦算不了什么。
quotes.author: Charles Dickens

quotes.en: It is never too late to be what you might have been.
quotes.zh: 成为你本可以成为的人，永远不晚。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: What do we live for, if it is not to make life less difficult to each other?
quotes.zh: 我们活着，若不是为了让彼此的生活少些艰难，又是为了什么？
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: The growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts.
quotes.zh: 世界日益向善，部分要归功于那些未被载入史册的举动。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: Nothing is so good as it seems beforehand.
quotes.zh: 没有一件事，能像事前看起来那么好。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: The strongest principle of growth lies in human choice.
quotes.zh: 成长最强大的动力，在于人的选择。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: Our dead are never dead to us, until we have forgotten them.
quotes.zh: 只要我们还没忘记，逝者就从未真正离开我们。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: A difference of taste in jokes is a great strain on the affections.
quotes.zh: 对笑话的品味不同，会给感情带来很大的负担。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: Only in the agony of parting do we look into the depths of love.
quotes.zh: 只有在离别的痛楚里，我们才看清爱的深处。
quotes.author: George Eliot

quotes.en: I am no bird; and no net ensnares me; I am a free human being with an independent will.
quotes.zh: 我不是鸟，也没有网能困住我；我是一个有独立意志的自由人。
quotes.author: Charlotte Brontë

quotes.en: Life appears to me too short to be spent in nursing animosity or registering wrongs.
quotes.zh: 在我看来，人生太短，不该用来记恨和记账。
quotes.author: Charlotte Brontë

quotes.en: I would always rather be happy than dignified.
quotes.zh: 我宁愿快乐，也不愿端着架子。
quotes.author: Charlotte Brontë

quotes.en: Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same.
quotes.zh: 不管我们的灵魂是由什么构成的，他的和我的是一样的。
quotes.author: Emily Brontë

quotes.en: He's more myself than I am.
quotes.zh: 他比我更像我自己。
quotes.author: Emily Brontë

quotes.en: Oh, what a tangled web we weave, when first we practise to deceive!
quotes.zh: 我们一旦开始欺骗，就织出一张多么纠缠的网！
quotes.author: Walter Scott

quotes.en: Breathes there the man with soul so dead, who never to himself hath said, this is my own, my native land!
quotes.zh: 可有谁的心灵死到如此地步，从未对自己说过：这是我的故土！
quotes.author: Walter Scott
quotes.source: The Lay of the Last Minstrel

quotes.en: War's a game, which, were their subjects wise, kings would not play at.
quotes.zh: 战争是一场游戏，若臣民足够明智，君王就不敢玩。
quotes.author: Walter Scott

quotes.en: Love rules the court, the camp, the grove, and men below, and saints above.
quotes.zh: 爱统治着宫廷、营地与树林，统治着下界的人，也统治着天上的圣者。
quotes.author: Walter Scott
quotes.source: The Lay of the Last Minstrel

quotes.en: All men who have turned out worth anything have had the chief hand in their own education.
quotes.zh: 凡是有所成就的人，都曾是自己教育的主要负责人。
quotes.author: Walter Scott

quotes.en: The world is a looking-glass, and gives back to every man the reflection of his own face.
quotes.zh: 世界是一面镜子，给每个人映出他自己那张脸。
quotes.author: William Makepeace Thackeray

quotes.en: Vanity Fair is a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions.
quotes.zh: 名利场是个极其虚荣、邪恶又愚蠢的地方，充满各种骗术、虚伪和做作。
quotes.author: William Makepeace Thackeray

quotes.en: Mother is the name for God in the lips and hearts of little children.
quotes.zh: 母亲，是小孩子嘴上和心里对上帝的称呼。
quotes.author: William Makepeace Thackeray

quotes.en: A good laugh is sunshine in a house.
quotes.zh: 一阵爽朗的笑声，是屋里的一片阳光。
quotes.author: William Makepeace Thackeray

quotes.en: To travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive.
quotes.zh: 满怀希望地旅行，比到达目的地更好。
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.en: The world is so full of a number of things, I'm sure we should all be as happy as kings.
quotes.zh: 世界上有这么多事物，我相信我们都该像国王一样快乐。
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.en: I travel not to go anywhere, but to go.
quotes.zh: 我旅行不是为了去什么地方，而是为了走。
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
quotes.source: Travels with a Donkey in the Cévennes

quotes.en: You cannot run away from weakness; you must some time fight it out or perish.
quotes.zh: 你无法逃避自己的软弱；总有一天你要与之搏斗，否则只能消亡。
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.en: It is better to lose health like a spendthrift than to waste it like a miser.
quotes.zh: 像挥霍者那样花掉健康，也好过像守财奴那样把它省着浪费。
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.en: A friend is a gift you give yourself.
quotes.zh: 朋友，是你送给自己的一份礼物。
quotes.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

quotes.en: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.
quotes.zh: 我们都在阴沟里，但仍有人仰望星空。
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.en: To live is the rarest thing in the world.
quotes.zh: 真正地活着，是世上最稀有的事。
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde
quotes.source: The Soul of Man under Socialism

quotes.en: The truth is rarely pure and never simple.
quotes.zh: 真相很少纯粹，也从不简单。
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.en: The books that the world calls immoral are books that show the world its own shame.
quotes.zh: 世人斥为不道德的书，正是让世界看见自身羞耻的书。
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.en: Nowadays people know the price of everything and the value of nothing.
quotes.zh: 如今人们知道一切东西的价格，却不知道任何东西的价值。
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.en: Experience is simply the name we give our mistakes.
quotes.zh: 经验，不过是我们给错误起的名字。
quotes.author: Oscar Wilde

quotes.en: Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
quotes.zh: 幸福的家庭都是相似的，不幸的家庭各有各的不幸。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.
quotes.zh: 人人都想改变世界，却没人想改变自己。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: There is no greatness where there is no simplicity, goodness and truth.
quotes.zh: 没有质朴、善良与真实，就没有伟大。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: We can know only that we know nothing. And that is the highest degree of human wisdom.
quotes.zh: 我们只能知道自己一无所知。而这正是人类智慧的最高境界。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: Everything I know, I know only because I love.
quotes.zh: 我所知道的一切，都只因为我爱。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: Music is the shorthand of emotion.
quotes.zh: 音乐是情感的速记。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: Kings are the slaves of history.
quotes.zh: 君王是历史的奴隶。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: If we admit that human life can be ruled by reason, the possibility of life is destroyed.
quotes.zh: 如果我们承认人生可由理性支配，那么生活的可能性就被毁掉了。
quotes.author: Leo Tolstoy

quotes.en: The mystery of human existence lies not in just staying alive, but in finding something to live for.
quotes.zh: 人类存在的奥秘不在于只是活着，而在于找到值得为之而活的东西。
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.en: Man is a mystery. It needs to be unravelled, and if you spend your whole life unraveling it, don't say that you've wasted time.
quotes.zh: 人是一个谜。这个谜需要解开，哪怕你花上一生去解，也别说自己浪费了时间。
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.en: Beauty will save the world.
quotes.zh: 美将拯救世界。
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.en: If there is no God, everything is permitted.
quotes.zh: 如果没有上帝，那就什么都可以做。
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.en: The soul is healed by being with children.
quotes.zh: 与孩子相处，灵魂会得到治愈。
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.en: Pain and suffering are always inevitable for a large intelligence and a deep heart.
quotes.zh: 对于广大的智识和深沉的心，痛苦与磨难总是不可避免的。
quotes.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

quotes.en: Knowledge is of no value unless you put it into practice.
quotes.zh: 知识若不付诸实践，就没有价值。
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.en: Don't tell me the moon is shining; show me the glint of light on broken glass.
quotes.zh: 别告诉我月亮在发光，给我看碎玻璃上那一闪的光。
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.en: Any idiot can face a crisis; it's this day-to-day living that wears you out.
quotes.zh: 傻瓜也能应付危机；真正把人耗垮的是日复一日的生活。
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.en: Medicine is my lawful wife, and literature is my mistress.
quotes.zh: 医学是我合法的妻子，文学是我的情人。
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.en: There is no national science, just as there is no national multiplication table.
quotes.zh: 没有国家的科学，就像没有国家的乘法表。
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.en: If you want to work on your art, work on your life.
quotes.zh: 想打磨你的艺术，就去打磨你的生活。
quotes.author: Anton Chekhov

quotes.en: A thousand words will not leave so deep an impression as one deed.
quotes.zh: 千言万语，不如一个行动留下的印象深。
quotes.author: Henrik Ibsen

quotes.en: The strongest man in the world is he who stands most alone.
quotes.zh: 世上最强的人，是站得最孤独的那一个。
quotes.author: Henrik Ibsen

quotes.en: You should never wear your best trousers when you go out to fight for freedom and truth.
quotes.zh: 为自由和真理而战时，千万别穿你最好的裤子。
quotes.author: Henrik Ibsen

quotes.en: A community is like a ship; everyone ought to be prepared to take the helm.
quotes.zh: 社会像一条船，人人都该准备好掌舵。
quotes.author: Henrik Ibsen

quotes.en: To live is to war with trolls in the vaults of heart and brain.
quotes.zh: 活着，就是与心底和脑海深处的小妖作战。
quotes.author: Henrik Ibsen

quotes.en: Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.
quotes.zh: 生活只能向后理解，却必须向前过。
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard

quotes.en: Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom.
quotes.zh: 焦虑，是自由带来的眩晕。
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard

quotes.en: The most common form of despair is not being who you are.
quotes.zh: 最常见的绝望，是不做自己。
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard

quotes.en: To dare is to lose one's footing momentarily. Not to dare is to lose oneself.
quotes.zh: 敢于冒险，只是暂时失去立足点；不敢冒险，却是失去自己。
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard

quotes.en: Purity of heart is to will one thing.
quotes.zh: 心的纯洁，就是只愿一件事。
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.source: Purity of Heart Is to Will One Thing

quotes.en: The crowd is untruth.
quotes.zh: 人群即虚妄。
quotes.author: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.source: The Point of View for My Work as an Author

quotes.en: The philosophers have only interpreted the world in various ways; the point, however, is to change it.
quotes.zh: 哲学家们只是用不同方式解释世界，问题在于改变世界。
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.en: Workers of the world, unite! You have nothing to lose but your chains.
quotes.zh: 全世界劳动者，联合起来！你们失去的只是锁链。
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.en: Religion is the opium of the people.
quotes.zh: 宗教是人民的鸦片。
quotes.author: Karl Marx
quotes.source: Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right

quotes.en: History repeats itself, first as tragedy, second as farce.
quotes.zh: 历史会重演，第一次是悲剧，第二次是闹剧。
quotes.author: Karl Marx
quotes.source: The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte

quotes.en: From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs.
quotes.zh: 各尽所能，按需分配。
quotes.author: Karl Marx

quotes.en: The only freedom which deserves the name is that of pursuing our own good in our own way.
quotes.zh: 唯一配得上自由之名的，是按自己的方式追求自己的善。
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.en: He who knows only his own side of the case knows little of that.
quotes.zh: 只知道自己这一方论据的人，对这一方也所知甚少。
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.en: A person may cause evil to others not only by his actions but by his inaction.
quotes.zh: 一个人不仅能以行动害人，也能以不作为害人。
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.en: The despotism of custom is everywhere the standing hindrance to human advancement.
quotes.zh: 习俗的专制，处处都是人类进步的长期障碍。
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.en: Better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.
quotes.zh: 做个不满足的人，胜过做头满足的猪；做不满足的苏格拉底，胜过做满足的傻瓜。
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.en: Ask yourself whether you are happy, and you cease to be so.
quotes.zh: 你一旦问自己是否幸福，你就不再幸福了。
quotes.author: John Stuart Mill

quotes.en: The pursuit of perfection is the pursuit of sweetness and light.
quotes.zh: 追求完美，就是追求甜美与光明。
quotes.author: Matthew Arnold

quotes.en: Culture is the best which has been thought and said in the world.
quotes.zh: 文化，是世上被思考过、被说过的最好的东西。
quotes.author: Matthew Arnold

quotes.en: Who saw life steadily, and saw it whole.
quotes.zh: 他稳稳地看取人生，看到它的整体。
quotes.author: Matthew Arnold

quotes.en: Poetry is at bottom a criticism of life.
quotes.zh: 诗，归根结底是对人生的批评。
quotes.author: Matthew Arnold

quotes.en: The highest reward for a person's toil is not what they get for it, but what they become by it.
quotes.zh: 一个人辛劳的最高回报，不是从中得到什么，而是因此成为什么。
quotes.author: John Ruskin

quotes.en: Quality is never an accident; it is always the result of intelligent effort.
quotes.zh: 品质从不是偶然，它永远是明智努力的结果。
quotes.author: John Ruskin

quotes.en: Fine art is that in which the hand, the head, and the heart of man go together.
quotes.zh: 美好的艺术，是手、脑与心共同参与的艺术。
quotes.author: John Ruskin

quotes.en: Mountains are the beginning and the end of all natural scenery.
quotes.zh: 山峦是一切自然风景的起点与终点。
quotes.author: John Ruskin

quotes.en: Poetry is the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings.
quotes.zh: 诗，是强烈感情的自发流露。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth

quotes.en: The child is father of the man.
quotes.zh: 孩子是成人之父。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth

quotes.en: I wandered lonely as a cloud.
quotes.zh: 我像一朵云那样孤独地飘荡。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth
quotes.source: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud

quotes.en: Getting and spending, we lay waste our powers.
quotes.zh: 在获取与花费中，我们浪费了自己的力量。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth
quotes.source: The World Is Too Much With Us

quotes.en: Nature never did betray the heart that loved her.
quotes.zh: 自然从不辜负爱她的心。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth
quotes.source: Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey

quotes.en: Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting.
quotes.zh: 我们的出生，不过是一场睡眠和一场遗忘。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth

quotes.en: Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive.
quotes.zh: 能活在那样的黎明，真是幸福。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth

quotes.en: What we have loved, others will love, and we will teach them how.
quotes.zh: 我们爱过的东西，别人也会爱，而我们将教他们如何去爱。
quotes.author: William Wordsworth

quotes.en: Water, water, every where, nor any drop to drink.
quotes.zh: 水啊，水啊，到处都是，却没有一滴能喝。
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
quotes.source: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

quotes.en: A sadder and a wiser man, he rose the morrow morn.
quotes.zh: 第二天清晨，他起身时更悲伤，也更明智了。
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
quotes.source: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

quotes.en: He prayeth best, who loveth best all things both great and small.
quotes.zh: 最懂得爱的人祈祷得最好，他爱一切伟大与渺小之物。
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
quotes.source: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

quotes.en: In Xanadu did Kubla Khan a stately pleasure-dome decree.
quotes.zh: 忽必烈在仙那度下令建造一座宏伟的欢愉之殿。
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge

quotes.en: Poetry is the best words in the best order.
quotes.zh: 诗，是以最好的次序排列的最好的词。
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge

quotes.en: No man was ever yet a great poet, without being at the same time a profound philosopher.
quotes.zh: 没有谁能在不是深刻哲人的同时，成为伟大的诗人。
quotes.author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge

quotes.en: Beauty is truth, truth beauty — that is all ye know on earth, and all ye need to know.
quotes.zh: 美即是真，真即是美——这就是你们在世上所知道的，也是你们需要知道的全部。
quotes.author: John Keats

quotes.en: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever.
quotes.zh: 美的东西，是永恒的喜悦。
quotes.author: John Keats

quotes.en: The poetry of earth is never dead.
quotes.zh: 大地的诗意永不消亡。
quotes.author: John Keats

quotes.en: Much have I travelled in the realms of gold.
quotes.zh: 我曾在金色的国度里远游。
quotes.author: John Keats
quotes.source: On First Looking into Chapman's Homer

quotes.en: Heard melodies are sweet, but those unheard are sweeter.
quotes.zh: 听得见的旋律是甜的，听不见的更甜。
quotes.author: John Keats

quotes.en: Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness.
quotes.zh: 雾霭与成熟果实的季节。
quotes.author: John Keats

quotes.en: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
quotes.zh: 冬天来了，春天还会远吗？
quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

quotes.en: O wild West Wind, thou breath of Autumn's being.
quotes.zh: 啊，狂野的西风，你是秋的气息。
quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

quotes.en: Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world.
quotes.zh: 诗人是世界未被承认的立法者。
quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

quotes.en: A man, to be greatly good, must imagine intensely and comprehensively.
quotes.zh: 一个人要真正善良，必须强烈而广博地想象。
quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

quotes.en: Our sweetest songs are those that tell of saddest thought.
quotes.zh: 我们最甜的歌，唱的是最悲伤的思绪。
quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

quotes.en: Nothing in the world is single; all things by a law divine in one another's being mingle.
quotes.zh: 世上没有孤立之物；万物按神圣的法则彼此交融。
quotes.author: Percy Bysshe Shelley

quotes.en: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climes and starry skies.
quotes.zh: 她走在美的光影里，像无云晴夜布满星辰。
quotes.author: Lord Byron

quotes.en: There is a pleasure in the pathless woods.
quotes.zh: 无路可循的森林里，自有一种乐趣。
quotes.author: Lord Byron

quotes.en: I love not man the less, but Nature more.
quotes.zh: 我并非爱人类更少，而是爱自然更多。
quotes.author: Lord Byron

quotes.en: When we two parted in silence and tears.
quotes.zh: 当我们两人在沉默与泪水中分别。
quotes.author: Lord Byron

quotes.en: All who joy would win must share it; happiness was born a twin.
quotes.zh: 想赢得欢乐的人都必须分享；幸福生来就是一对双胞胎。
quotes.author: Lord Byron

quotes.en: The thorns which I have reaped are of the tree I planted.
quotes.zh: 我收获的荆棘，都来自我自己种下的那棵树。
quotes.author: Lord Byron

quotes.en: To see a world in a grain of sand and a heaven in a wild flower.
quotes.zh: 从一粒沙里看见一个世界，从一朵野花里看见一座天堂。
quotes.author: William Blake

quotes.en: A truth that's told with bad intent beats all the lies you can invent.
quotes.zh: 怀着恶意说出的真话，胜过你能编造的一切谎言。
quotes.author: William Blake

quotes.en: The road of excess leads to the palace of wisdom.
quotes.zh: 放纵之路，通往智慧的宫殿。
quotes.author: William Blake
quotes.source: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell

quotes.en: Energy is eternal delight.
quotes.zh: 能量是永恒的欢愉。
quotes.author: William Blake
quotes.source: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell

quotes.en: If the doors of perception were cleansed everything would appear to man as it is, infinite.
quotes.zh: 若知觉之门被洗净，万物在人眼中就会显现其本来面目：无限。
quotes.author: William Blake
quotes.source: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell

quotes.en: He who desires but acts not, breeds pestilence.
quotes.zh: 只空想而不行动的人，会滋生瘟疫。
quotes.author: William Blake
quotes.source: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell

quotes.en: My love is like a red, red rose, that's newly sprung in June.
quotes.zh: 我的爱人像一朵红红的玫瑰，六月里刚刚绽放。
quotes.author: Robert Burns

quotes.en: Man's inhumanity to man makes countless thousands mourn.
quotes.zh: 人对人的不人道，让无数千人哀哭。
quotes.author: Robert Burns

quotes.en: But pleasures are like poppies spread: you seize the flower, its bloom is shed.
quotes.zh: 欢乐像盛开的罂粟：你摘下花朵，花瓣就落了。
quotes.author: Robert Burns

quotes.en: The best laid schemes of mice and men often go awry.
quotes.zh: 老鼠和人最周密的计划，也常常落空。
quotes.author: Robert Burns

quotes.en: 'Tis better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.
quotes.zh: 爱过又失去，胜过从未爱过。
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson

quotes.en: Theirs not to reason why, theirs but to do and die.
quotes.zh: 他们的本分不是追问为什么，而是去做、去死。
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
quotes.source: The Charge of the Light Brigade

quotes.en: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
quotes.zh: 去奋斗，去探索，去发现，永不屈服。
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson

quotes.en: I am a part of all that I have met.
quotes.zh: 我是我所遇见的一切的一部分。
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson

quotes.en: The old order changeth, yielding place to new.
quotes.zh: 旧的秩序正在改变，让位给新的。
quotes.author: Alfred, Lord Tennyson

quotes.en: Ah, but a man's reach should exceed his grasp, or what's a heaven for?
quotes.zh: 人的追求应当超出他所能掌握的范围，否则天堂是做什么用的？
quotes.author: Robert Browning

quotes.en: Grow old along with me! The best is yet to be.
quotes.zh: 和我一起变老吧！最好的还在后面。
quotes.author: Robert Browning

quotes.en: God's in his heaven — all's right with the world.
quotes.zh: 上帝在他的天堂里，世间一切安好。
quotes.author: Robert Browning

quotes.en: The life so short, the craft so long to learn.
quotes.zh: 生命如此短暂，技艺却要学这么久。
quotes.author: Geoffrey Chaucer

quotes.en: If gold rusts, what will iron do?
quotes.zh: 金子都会生锈，铁又会怎样？
quotes.author: Geoffrey Chaucer

quotes.en: Time and tide wait for no man.
quotes.zh: 时间与潮水都不等人。
quotes.author: Geoffrey Chaucer

quotes.en: He was a true, perfect, gentle knight.
quotes.zh: 他是一位真正完美、温厚的骑士。
quotes.author: Geoffrey Chaucer

quotes.en: Abandon all hope, ye who enter here.
quotes.zh: 进来的人，放弃一切希望吧。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: Midway upon the journey of our life I found myself within a forest dark.
quotes.zh: 在人生旅程的中途，我发现自己置身一片幽暗的森林。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: There is no greater sorrow than to recall our time of joy in wretchedness.
quotes.zh: 最大的悲哀，是在痛苦中回想往日的欢乐。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: The love that moves the sun and the other stars.
quotes.zh: 那推动太阳与群星的爱。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: Consider your origin: you were not made to live as brutes, but to follow virtue and knowledge.
quotes.zh: 想想你们的出身：你们生来不是为了像野兽那样活，而是为了追求美德与知识。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: Nature is the art of God.
quotes.zh: 自然是上帝的艺术。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: A great flame follows a little spark.
quotes.zh: 一点小火星，能燃起熊熊大火。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: Love is the seed in you of every virtue.
quotes.zh: 爱，是你心中一切美德的种子。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: Without hope we live in desire.
quotes.zh: 没有希望，我们便活在欲望里。
quotes.author: Dante Alighieri

quotes.en: A short cut to riches is to subtract from our desires.
quotes.zh: 通往富足的捷径，是减少我们的欲望。
quotes.author: Petrarch

quotes.en: Sameness is the mother of disgust, variety the cure.
quotes.zh: 千篇一律是厌倦之母，变化才是解药。
quotes.author: Petrarch

quotes.en: Rarely do great beauty and great virtue dwell together.
quotes.zh: 伟大的美与伟大的德行，很少同住一处。
quotes.author: Petrarch

quotes.en: I find no peace, and all my war is done.
quotes.zh: 我找不到安宁，而我的战争已经结束。
quotes.author: Petrarch

quotes.en: In the land of the blind, the one-eyed man is king.
quotes.zh: 在盲人之国，独眼者就是国王。
quotes.author: Erasmus

quotes.en: Prevention is better than cure.
quotes.zh: 预防胜过治疗。
quotes.author: Erasmus

quotes.en: War is delightful to those who have had no experience of it.
quotes.zh: 对没经历过战争的人，战争是令人愉快的。
quotes.author: Erasmus

quotes.en: Fools are without number.
quotes.zh: 愚人多得数不清。
quotes.author: Erasmus

quotes.en: He who allows oppression shares the crime.
quotes.zh: 纵容压迫的人，与压迫者同罪。
quotes.author: Erasmus

quotes.en: It is better to be feared than loved, if you cannot be both.
quotes.zh: 若不能两者兼得，令人畏惧比受人爱戴更安全。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: The ends justify the means.
quotes.zh: 只要目的正当，手段就可以成立。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: Everyone sees what you appear to be, few experience what you really are.
quotes.zh: 人人都看见你表面的样子，很少有人体会你真实的样子。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: Never was anything great achieved without danger.
quotes.zh: 没有危险，就从未成就过任何伟大的事。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: Whoever desires constant success must change his conduct with the times.
quotes.zh: 想一直成功的人，必须随时代改变自己的做法。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: Men judge generally more by the eye than by the hand.
quotes.zh: 人们判断事物，多半靠眼睛，而不是靠亲手了解。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: The first method for estimating the intelligence of a ruler is to look at the men he has around him.
quotes.zh: 判断一个统治者是否明智，最直接的方法是看他身边是什么人。
quotes.author: Niccolò Machiavelli

quotes.en: The truth may be stretched thin, but it never breaks.
quotes.zh: 真相可以被拉得很薄，却永远不会断。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: He who sings scares away his woes.
quotes.zh: 唱歌的人，能把忧愁吓跑。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: All sorrows are less with bread.
quotes.zh: 有面包相伴，一切悲伤都会轻一些。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: The pen is the tongue of the mind.
quotes.zh: 笔，是心灵的舌头。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: There is no book so bad that it does not have something good in it.
quotes.zh: 再坏的书，也不会一无是处。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: To be prepared is half the victory.
quotes.zh: 有备而来，就赢了一半。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: Fortune leaves always some door open to come at a remedy.
quotes.zh: 命运总会留下一扇门，让人找到补救的办法。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: He who loses wealth loses much; he who loses a friend loses more; but he who loses courage loses all.
quotes.zh: 失去财富损失很大，失去朋友损失更大，失去勇气就失去了一切。
quotes.author: Miguel de Cervantes

quotes.en: I die the king's good servant, but God's first.
quotes.zh: 我死去时是国王的好仆人，但首先是上帝的子民。
quotes.author: Thomas More

quotes.en: The ordinary acts of life are the best schools of virtue.
quotes.zh: 日常生活的一举一动，是培养美德最好的学校。
quotes.author: Thomas More

quotes.en: The things that we love tell us what we are.
quotes.zh: 我们所爱的东西，说明了我们是什么样的人。
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas

quotes.en: Beware the man of one book.
quotes.zh: 要当心只读一本书的人。
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas

quotes.en: Grace does not destroy nature, but perfects it.
quotes.zh: 恩典不摧毁自然，而是使之完善。
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas

quotes.en: Justice is a certain rectitude of mind whereby a man does what he ought to do.
quotes.zh: 正义是心灵的一种正直，使人去做他应当做的事。
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas

quotes.en: The world is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page.
quotes.zh: 世界是一本书，不旅行的人只读了其中一页。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: Patience is the companion of wisdom.
quotes.zh: 耐心是智慧的伴侣。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: Thou hast made us for thyself, O Lord, and our heart is restless until it rests in thee.
quotes.zh: 主啊，你为自己创造了我们，我们的心不得安宁，直到安息于你。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: What then is time? If no one asks me, I know; if I wish to explain it, I know not.
quotes.zh: 那么时间是什么？没人问时我知道，要解释时我又不知道。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: Love and do what you will.
quotes.zh: 爱吧，然后做你愿意做的。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.source: Homilies on the First Epistle of John

quotes.en: The mind commands the body and is obeyed; the mind commands itself and is resisted.
quotes.zh: 心灵命令身体，身体服从；心灵命令自己，却遭到抵抗。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: Hope has two beautiful daughters: anger and courage.
quotes.zh: 希望有两个美丽的女儿：愤怒与勇气。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: It was pride that changed angels into devils; it is humility that makes men as angels.
quotes.zh: 是骄傲把天使变成魔鬼，是谦卑使人近似天使。
quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo

quotes.en: The wound is the place where the light enters you.
quotes.zh: 伤口，正是光进入你的地方。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: What you seek is seeking you.
quotes.zh: 你所寻找的，也在寻找你。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: Don't grieve. Anything you lose comes round in another form.
quotes.zh: 不要悲伤。你失去的一切，都会以另一种形式回来。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: Raise your words, not your voice. It is rain that grows flowers, not thunder.
quotes.zh: 提高你的言语，而不是你的嗓门。催开花朵的是雨，不是雷。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: Silence is the language of God; all else is poor translation.
quotes.zh: 沉默是上帝的语言，其余一切都是拙劣的翻译。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: Let yourself be silently drawn by the strange pull of what you really love.
quotes.zh: 让自己被真正所爱之物的奇异引力默默牵引。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: Come, come, whoever you are.
quotes.zh: 来吧，来吧，无论你是谁。
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.en: Human beings are members of a whole, in creation of one essence and soul.
quotes.zh: 人类是一个整体中的成员，在创世中同出一源、同一灵魂。
quotes.author: Saadi

quotes.en: Whoever is not grateful for a small favor will not be grateful for a great one.
quotes.zh: 对小恩惠不知感恩的人，也不会对大的恩惠感恩。
quotes.author: Saadi

quotes.en: Two things indicate weakness in a man: to be silent when it is proper to speak, and to speak when it is proper to be silent.
quotes.zh: 两件事显出人的软弱：该说话时沉默，该沉默时说话。
quotes.author: Saadi

quotes.en: I complained of my lack of shoes until I saw a man without feet.
quotes.zh: 我曾抱怨没有鞋穿，直到看见一个没有脚的人。
quotes.author: Saadi

quotes.en: The world is a bridge; pass over it, but build no house upon it.
quotes.zh: 世界是一座桥；走过去，但别在上面盖房子。
quotes.author: Saadi

quotes.en: The Moving Finger writes; and, having writ, moves on.
quotes.zh: 书写的手指写下便继续前行。
quotes.author: Omar Khayyam

quotes.en: A book of verses underneath the bough, a jug of wine, a loaf of bread, and thou.
quotes.zh: 树荫下一卷诗，一壶酒，一块面包，还有你。
quotes.author: Omar Khayyam

quotes.en: Ah, make the most of what we yet may spend, before we too into the dust descend.
quotes.zh: 啊，趁我们还能花费，尽情享用吧，趁我们尚未化为尘土。
quotes.author: Omar Khayyam

quotes.en: Knowledge without action is arrogance.
quotes.zh: 没有行动的知识，是傲慢。
quotes.author: Al-Ghazali

quotes.en: Man is social by nature.
quotes.zh: 人天生是社会性的。
quotes.author: Ibn Khaldun

quotes.en: The past resembles the future more than one drop of water resembles another.
quotes.zh: 过去与未来的相似，胜过一滴水与另一滴水的相似。
quotes.author: Ibn Khaldun

quotes.en: Geography is destiny.
quotes.zh: 地理即命运。
quotes.author: Ibn Khaldun

quotes.en: Lead me from the unreal to the real.
quotes.zh: 请引领我从虚妄走向真实。
quotes.author: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad

quotes.en: From darkness lead me to light.
quotes.zh: 请引领我从黑暗走向光明。
quotes.author: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad

quotes.en: From death lead me to immortality.
quotes.zh: 请引领我从死亡走向不朽。
quotes.author: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad

quotes.en: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
quotes.zh: 起来，觉醒，不达目标绝不停止。
quotes.author: Katha Upanishad

quotes.en: That thou art.
quotes.zh: 你就是那个。
quotes.author: Chandogya Upanishad

quotes.en: The knowing Self is not born, nor does it die.
quotes.zh: 有知的自我既不生，也不死。
quotes.author: Katha Upanishad

quotes.en: A man is great by deeds, not by birth.
quotes.zh: 人的伟大在于行为，而不在出身。
quotes.author: Chanakya

quotes.en: Education is the best friend.
quotes.zh: 教育是最好的朋友。
quotes.author: Chanakya

quotes.en: A person should not be too honest; straight trees are cut first.
quotes.zh: 人不能太耿直；笔直的树总是最先被砍。
quotes.author: Chanakya

quotes.en: As soon as fear approaches near, attack and destroy it.
quotes.zh: 恐惧一靠近，就攻击并消灭它。
quotes.author: Chanakya

quotes.en: Look to this day, for it is life.
quotes.zh: 看好今天，因为它就是生命。
quotes.author: Kalidasa

quotes.en: Yesterday is but a dream, and tomorrow is only a vision.
quotes.zh: 昨天不过是一场梦，明天只是一幅幻景。
quotes.author: Kalidasa

quotes.en: Look well therefore to this day.
quotes.zh: 因此，好好看重今天。
quotes.author: Kalidasa

quotes.en: The way of the samurai is found in death.
quotes.zh: 武士之道，存在于直面死亡之中。
quotes.author: Yamamoto Tsunetomo

quotes.en: Conquer anger by love; conquer evil by good.
quotes.zh: 以爱战胜愤怒，以善战胜邪恶。
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.en: Though one should conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle, he who conquers himself is the greatest victor.
quotes.zh: 即使在战场上战胜千万人，能战胜自己的人才是最伟大的胜利者。
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.en: Let us live happily, free from hatred among those who hate.
quotes.zh: 让我们快乐地活着，在仇恨者中间不怀仇恨。
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.en: Health is the greatest gift, contentment the greatest wealth, a trusted friend the best relative.
quotes.zh: 健康是最好的礼物，知足是最大的财富，可信的朋友是最好的亲人。
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.en: Better to live one day wise and meditative than a hundred years foolish and uncontrolled.
quotes.zh: 明智而静观地活一天，胜过愚昧而放纵地活一百年。
quotes.author: Buddha

quotes.en: The superior man is slow in words but quick in action.
quotes.zh: 君子言语迟缓，行动敏捷。
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.en: When I walk along with two others, they may serve me as my teachers.
quotes.zh: 与两个人同行，他们也可以做我的老师。
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.en: It is not the failure of others to appreciate your abilities that should trouble you, but your own failure to appreciate theirs.
quotes.zh: 该困扰你的不是别人不赏识你的才能，而是你不懂得赏识别人的才能。
quotes.author: Confucius

quotes.en: The highest good is like water.
quotes.zh: 最高的善，像水一样。
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.en: The softest thing in the world overcomes the hardest.
quotes.zh: 天下最柔软的东西，能胜过最坚硬的东西。
quotes.author: Laozi

quotes.en: Knowing when to stop is the way to avoid danger.
quotes.zh: 懂得何时停下，才是避免危险的办法。
quotes.author: Laozi
